<div class="study-label">Actuarial research note · August 2026</div>

The study quantifies self-reported internet interruptions as an operating-risk exposure, validates a parsimonious actuarial model against a machine-learning challenger, and translates the evidence into conditional planning provisions.

## What the project measures

The empirical layer estimates internet-disruption occurrence and conditional duration for formal businesses represented by the 2024 survey. The actuarial layer decomposes the loss cost into disruption probability, probability of a positive loss given disruption, and mean positive severity. The forward layer applies explicit stress, growth and prudence assumptions from 2027 to 2031.

![The three-stage actuarial internet-loss chain](artifacts/public/figures/actuarial-loss-chain.png){fig-alt="Horizontal bars for disruption probability, positive loss probability conditional on disruption, and mean severity conditional on positive loss."}

The calibrated expected loss ratio is **`r fmt_ratio_pct(calibration$expected_loss_ratio)`**. Applied to 10 million TND of annual-sales exposure, the 2027 persistent-condition scenario produces an expected economic loss of **`r fmt_tnd(persistent_2027$expected_economic_loss_tnd)`** and a risk-adjusted planning provision of **`r fmt_tnd(persistent_2027$risk_adjusted_provision_tnd)`**.

::: {.callout-important title="This is not a loss estimate for an operator"}
The business survey does not identify the internet provider. It cannot show that Tunisie Télécom, Ooredoo Tunisia, Orange Tunisia or another provider caused an individual business loss. Official INT and RIPE Atlas evidence is kept in a separate contextual layer.
:::

## Why the result is actuarially useful

The project does not hide the weak part of the evidence. There are `r calibration$valid_loss_ratio_responses` usable loss-ratio answers among disrupted firms and only `r calibration$positive_loss_events` positive losses. That supports a transparent empirical calibration and bootstrap, but not a stable severity GLM. The model gate blocks unsupported precision.

## The AI contribution

A histogram gradient-boosting challenger is evaluated with repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. Its mean weighted AUC is **`r formatC(metric_value(ml_validation, "weighted_auc"), digits = 3, format = "f")`**, compared with **`r formatC(metric_value(validation, "weighted_auc"), digits = 3, format = "f")`** for the actuarial GLM. The challenger is not promoted because only `r evidence$disruption_events` events are available against a predeclared threshold of 200.

::: {.panel}
**Decision principle:** predictive metrics inform comparison; evidence sufficiency determines whether a model may be used. Feature importance is diagnostic, not causal.
:::

## Reproducible public boundary

Raw WBES microdata remain local. The public repository contains aggregate estimates, coefficients, validation summaries, assumptions, source checksums and figures. Automated checks prevent individual identifiers, annual sales and monetary loss records from entering public CSV files.
